name: Inspired Media
description:
Inspire(d) is an independent media company founded in 2007 in Decorah, Iowa. We create hyper-local positive news in print and online, featuring the people, places, and things that make our region great. We inspire our readers, while also promoting tourism, economic development, and town-pride.
We print Inspire(d) Magazine, our “experiment in positive news,” on a quarterly schedule – spring, summer, fall, winter.
Aryn Henning Nichols and Benji Nichols founded Inspire(d) shortly after they got married – 3000 copies of issue one rolled off the press October 4, 2007. Inspire(d) has now grown to print 13,000-16,500 magazines per issue, distributed free to more than 125 locations across our neck of the Driftless Region (Northeast Iowa, Southeast Minnesota, and Western Wisconsin) here in the Midwest.
It’s a two-person show at Inspire(d) Headquarters: Aryn is the editor and graphic designer and Benji heads up logistics and the ad sales department, but we’d be nothing without our fabulous contributors who hail from different areas across the region and beyond.
You can also follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and Pinterest, and make sure you don’t miss Inspire(d)’s companion podcast, Rhymes with Decorah, at www.decorah.fun. Produced by Benji Nichols (who brings a background in public radio and an excellent radio voice to the project), RWD is a fun way to learn a more about the communities we serve in the region (not just Decorah!) and the challenges we can all work together to overcome.
Thanks for being a part of this "experiment in positive news"!

name: Viroqua Area Schools
description:
Preparing Tomorrow’s Leaders Today
Viroqua Area Schools serves approximately 1,000 students across six schools including Viroqua Elementary School, Viroqua Middle School, Viroqua High School, and three public charter schools: Viroqua Area Montessori Charter School, Laurel High School, and Vernon County Better Futures High School. Viroqua is also home to a Waldorf School and the Youth Initiative High School that follow the Waldorf model of education.
Viroqua Area Schools
Viroqua Elementary, Middle, and High schools serve students in grades K-12 and offer a wide range of academic and extracurricular activities, including sports, music and drama programs, and clubs. The award-winning schools have a strong focus on college and career readiness with a variety of programs and resources to help students prepare for their future including a large number of advanced placement (AP) courses and dual enrollment courses with Western Technical College.
The Viroqua Area Montessori School (VAMS) is a public charter school that shares a campus with the Viroqua Elementary School and Viroqua Middle School. VAMS offers seven multi-age classrooms serving 4K through eighth-grade students following a traditional Montessori model.
Laurel High School is a public charter school serving students in grades 9-12. The curriculum at Laurel High School includes a variety of subjects such as math, science, English, social studies, and world languages. The school also offers advanced placement (AP) courses for students who wish to pursue college-level coursework and many independent studies that allow the students to explore their individual interests. In addition to traditional academic programs, Laurel High School offers several extracurricular activities for students to explore their interests and develop their skills. These activities include athletics, music, drama, and clubs focused on topics such as science, technology, and community service.
Better Futures High School is a public, alternative high school that is part of the Viroqua Area School District. The school serves students from four Vernon county schools who may have struggled in a traditional high school setting and offers a more personalized approach to learning. The school offers a more individualized approach with smaller class sizes and more one-on-one attention from teachers. They also have a focus on experiential learning with opportunities for internships, job shadowing, service-learning projects, and employment.

From Amish to jewelry makers, candy makers to antique dealers, they've all found a place in our historic building. We've had weddings, festivals, concerts, and plays in the courtyard over the years. We've watched kids grow up and people fall in love. We've greeted visitors from all over the world; locals who still remember the building when it was a car dealership, and scores of folks from around the state. All this, we've done as a family. Our "extended" family of multiple business-owners, artists, and restauranteurs who have come and gone from the Main Street Station store fronts are a valuable part of our history. Those still remaining have grown with us in their own right and the Viroqua Public Market holds great promise for future small business owners and entrepreneurs. We've watched the community of Viroqua grow and prosper, ever evolving into a more and more beautiful place to be. Thank you all for your continued support. We hope to serve you for many years to come.
